subject: wolf spider
title: A Wolf Spider Mom Carries Over 100 Babies on Her Back

scenes.text: This spider's back can be covered in a hundred moving eyes. They're her babies.
A wolf spider mother drags her egg sac everywhere, tied to the silk glands at her rear.
When the eggs hatch, the spiderlings climb up onto her back, sometimes more than a hundred of them.
They hold on to special knob-shaped hairs, living off leftover yolk.
She keeps hunting with them on board, for days or even weeks.
Only after their first molt do they climb off and scatter. Next time you see a fuzzy spider, look closer.

description:
Wolf spider mothers carry their egg sac attached to their spinnerets. After hatching, dozens to hundreds of spiderlings ride on her back, clinging to knob-shaped hairs and living largely off leftover yolk, for several days to weeks until they moult and disperse.
Would you let one walk past you?
first_comment: She even stops at water so the babies can hop off and drink. Cute or creepy?
